items.article: SANDAL season is officially over, and while you may not be ready to don winter boots just yet in this transitional weather, it’s still time to... SANDAL season is officially over, and while you may not be ready to don winter boots just yet in this transitional weather, it’s still time to rethink your footwear. While most of us have spent the last six months living in flip-flops, strappy sandals, and ballet flats, it’s time to swap our summer staples for more reliable footwear. Loafers have long been a wardrobe staple, and it’s easy to see why. Once considered a style reserved for smarter occasions, they’ve become a more versatile everyday option, and this season brings a whole host of fresh takes on the classic silhouette. But for all of the polished appeal, there’s one problem: they’re notoriously difficult to wear in. From stiff leather to unforgiving backs that rub at the heel, they can easily leave you reaching for blister plasters and finding a pair that look good and feel comfortable can be easier said than done.

items.article: While the immediate trigger for the CJP protest against the CEC was the Express investigation, the choice to hold the protest in Mumbai and on Gandhi Jayanti is deliberate The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will begin its much-anticipated ‘Jail Bharo Andolan’ against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park today . While the immediate trigger for the CJP protest against the CEC was the Express investigation , revealing the internal rift within the Election Commission, the choice to hold the protest in Mumbai is deliberate. Addressing a press conference in Mumbai on Thursday, Abhijeet Dipke explained why. “In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, BJP won only nine seats out of 48 seats. In the Assembly elections held six months later, the scenario changed altogether. How did this change happen?” he asked. “It is in this context that we have chosen to start the agitation from Mumbai,” Dipke said. Moreover, he explained in Marathi, “ Delhi che hi takth rakhto Maharashtra maza [Even the Delhi throne is guarded by Maharashtra].” For those unversed, in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP won only nine seats out of 28 contested. Along with its alliance partners Shiv Sena (7) and NCP (1), Mahayuti’s tally went up to 17 seats out of 48.

items.article: Tennis balls with handwritten messages on them have been batted into garden on two occasions It seems fans of Big Brother have been trying to meddle with this year's series by communicating messages to the housemates from the outside world. It's understood that TV show execs have now been forced to make major changes including to security for the remainder of the show. Pranksters have, on two occasions, been able to bat tennis balls into the garden in a bid to communicate with the housemates who are going into their third week. ITV has categorically ruled out that production has anything to do with the stunt, and that they have come from viewers of the iconic show. Housemates read the messages aloud on the balls before bosses ordered them indoors and put the house on lockdown while it was investigated. The first round of balls claimed that housemate Lynx had a girlfriend on the outside and falsely claimed there was another secret mole in the house, sending the cast into chaos.

items.article: The What Car? survey provides insight into 225 models from 30 brands across 16 fault categories. Here's which models drivers said are reliable. By FREDA LEWIS-STEMPEL, SENIOR MOTORING REPORTER Drivers have revealed which carmakers produce the most and least reliable vehicles in a huge survey of tens of thousands of motorists – and it's bad news for a Chinese SUV sales sensation. With Britons facing the highest diesel prices in UK history and rising petrol prices due to the Iran conflict, the last thing motorists need is for their car to break the bank in repair bills. Luckily, those shopping for a new car can turn to surveys where buyers give their honest, and sometimes hard-earned, feedback on how dependable their car is – and if they'd recommend it to their fellow drivers based on their own experiences. This year's What Car? Reliability Survey is one of the biggest car polls in the country, garnering feedback from 39,332 owners over the past two years. With it now more important than ever to choose a dependable car, the What Car? survey provides insight into 225 models from 30 brands across 16 fault categories.

items.article: A cause of death for the daughter of actor Chad Lowe, Fiona, has been revealed after she died aged 13. A cause of death for Chad Lowe’s daughter Fiona, who died at the age of 13, has been revealed. It was announced this week that Fiona had died , with her family saying they were ‘deeply heartbroken’ while paying tribute to their second daughter. Fiona, who was also the niece of Hollywood actor Rob Lowe, died at a hospital in Los Angeles on Tuesday, just weeks before she was due to celebrate her 14th birthday. The County of Los Angeles Medical Examiner has now revealed her manner of death to be suicide. She was pronounced dead at the hospital at 1:14am on September 29 and her body can now be released to the family. Alongside their statement on Wednesday confirming Fiona’s death, the Lowe family included details for the US 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline for those struggling with their mental health . Sharing the heartbreaking news, they said: ‘She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents.

For those of you who missed the first episode of The Celebrity Traitors last night, Claudia selected Maya Jama and Grant as her two traitors , with those two then permitted to pick their third option up in the turret. However, that choice was complicated somewhat by a rather big slip-up from the Swazi actor just moments after he'd been tapped on the shoulder at the round table, as when asked by Joe Lycett , he said twice that he was a traitor. It's difficult to see a way back for the 69-year-old after that, even if some celebrities have come to his defence, but two of the biggest names after him were James Acaster and Amol Rajan, one of whom will become the third traitor, while the other will have their game ended. items.article: Ghost in the Shell still defines cyberpunk sci-fi, and you can experience it now on YouTube. Before The Matrix, this anime imagined a chilling digital future Anime has never been short on landmark science fiction. Akira wrote the book on bridging cyberpunk and adult animation, while Neon Genesis Evangelion blended apocalyptic mech battles and psychological trauma into pure spectacle. The great Shinichiro Watanabe made a western in space with Cowboy Bebop , a sci-fi adventure unlike any other with its emphasis on noir jazz and existential melancholy that's still one of anime’s most enduring worlds. Before any of them even existed, it was sci-fi that birthed the industry thanks to Osamu Tezuka’s 1963 hit Astro Boy . Yet for all the incredible science fiction anime the industry has produced, none has stared so directly into the unsettling future of synthetic identity and digital consciousness quite like Ghost in the Shell . Mamoru Oshii’s 1995 classic remains one of anime’s crowning achievements, influencing everything from 1999’s The Matrix to 2009’s Avatar , and there’s no better time to confront its bleak technological future than now, while it’s free to watch on YouTube. Based on Masamune Shirow’s manga, Ghost in the Shell follows Major Motoko Kusanagi, a cybernetic government operative investigating a mysterious hacker known as the Puppet Master. items.text: Finland has a fix for nuclear waste
items.article: At least until the next ice age | World News After four and a half decades of planning, it took only ten hours to drill through the 1.9bn-year-old bedrock. Final digging began last month at Onkalo, a geological disposal facility (GDF) in Finland. It will be the resting place for 6,500 tonnes of hazardous nuclear waste. Sealed 400 metres beneath the earth, its radiation will remain contained for over 100,000 years. Since the infancy of nuclear power, scientists have debated how to safely dispose of its waste. GDFs are the gold standard, and Onkalo will be the first on Earth. Posiva, the firm that runs it, aims to have it ready by year’s end. It comes at a time of renewed enthusiasm for the nuclear industry, driven by the desire for carbon-free electricity and wars that have disrupted fossil-fuel supplies. Global nuclear-power output will double by 2050, reckons the UN’s International Atomic Energy Agency. France, Sweden and Slovakia are building reactors. Belgium, Italy and Poland hope to as well. About 70% of the world’s nuclear waste is currently held in cooling pools or in dry storage. These are vulnerable to decay and unstable weather. The volume of waste created is small: a typical reactor produces 25-30 tonnes of spent fuel per year, about 0.5% of Onkalo’s capacity. But for Israel to substantiate the claims, the Jewish nation will need to thoroughly investigate the incident and interrogate the co-pilot. That access has now become a possibility with the co-pilot being handed over by Saudi Arabia to the United Arab Emirates (UAE). While Israel doesn't have formal ties with Saudi Arabia, it has developed a warm relationship with the UAE. The UAE signed the Abraham Accords in 2020, recognising the Jewish state. Oman, the country to which the co-pilot belongs, doesn't recognise Israel and has no formal ties with it. items.text: How to see the Orionid meteor shower from Friday
items.article: Friday sees the start of the Orionid meteor shower as Earth passes through debris left behind by Halley’s Comet. It peaks later in October. One of the best-known meteor showers is now active until 7 November. The Orionids are particularly fast and can leave trails in the sky that last a few seconds after the meteor itself has gone. The display occurs at around the same time each year when the Earth passes through a trail of dust and debris left behind by Halley's Comet. The showers peak overnight from 21 to 22 October. The Orionids are particularly fast, entering the atmosphere at around 41 miles per second. As tiny particles from Halley's comet enter the Earth's atmosphere they heat up and produce streaks of light across the night sky that we see as meteors.
